name: Regent Phu Quoc
positioning: All-pool villa and suite resort on Long Beach on Phu Quoc island, Vietnam, with Japanese-French and Vietnamese dining and a spa with Bastien Gonzalez and Biologique Recherche treatments
best_for: Families or groups wanting multi-bedroom pool villas, many with a full kitchen
Couples wanting a beach stay with a private pool and personalised service

facts.text: The resort's design frames Phu Quoc's Long Beach.
The resort is in the Phu Quoc Marina Integrated Resort Complex.
Accommodation is all pool villas and suites.
Most of the villas and some of the suites come with a full kitchen.
Oku, the signature restaurant, serves contemporary Japanese-French cuisine and features an Omakase Atelier and Salon de Boeuf.
Rice Market celebrates rice, with rice and noodle dishes made with Vietnamese herbs, spices and recipes.
Ocean Club has a beach club feel, with rum-inspired cocktails and poolside lounging with ocean views.
Fu Bar has a gin-centric drink list and nightly sax jazz.
The spa has a Biologique Recherche facial suite.
Wellness therapies use golden alpha-quartz sand.
For children there are kids pools, an imagination zone, a playground and a mini-theatre zone.
Regent Phu Quoc was recognised in the MICHELIN Key List for 2025 and 2026.

highlights.text: Sky Pool Villas use a vertical villa concept in the Sky Wing, with panoramic resort views and a private infinity pool.
The spa has a Pedi:Mani:Cure Studio by podiatrist Bastien Gonzalez, focused on medical pedicures and manicures.
The in-room Refreshment Gallery, with alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, local artisanal coffee, tea and delicacies, is included.
The Three Bedroom Beach Pool Villa sits directly on the white sands of Long Beach, with a living and kitchen area and unobstructed sunset views.
Personal Havens are private spaces customised with your choice of food and drink, scent, music, books and bath menus.

considerations.text: The resort shares an integrated resort complex with the InterContinental next door and apartment blocks that were under construction.
Phu Quoc is less culture-rich than Vietnam's other regions; unless you want a pure beach holiday, consider combining a stay with a trip upcountry.
WhataHotel notes the remote island location requires flight connections.
